Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the District Differently Abled Welfare Officer.
Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the District Differently Abled Welfare Officer to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, and a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. National Identity Card of the Differently abled Bride and Groom.
2. Marriage Certificate.
3. Age Proof of Bride and Groom
4. Degree or Diploma Certificate Bride and(or) Groom
Summary: This scheme provides financial assistance to normal individuals marrying orthopedically differently abled persons. Its objective is to support and facilitate such marriages, promoting inclusivity and alleviating financial burdens.

Title: Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department-Incentive/Award of Prizes
Details: The scheme “Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department-Incentive/Award of Prizes” by the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, provides district-level prizes to students based on their performance in the 10th and 12th standard examinations. The incentives are given to one Boy and one Girl each from Adi Dravidar/ Tribal/ Adi Dravidar Converted to Christianity who have secured the highest mark.
Benefits:
1. 10+2 Examination: ₹3,000/-.
2. 10th Std. First Prize: ₹1,000/-.
3. 10th Std. Second Prize: ₹5,00/-.
4. 10th Std. Third Prize: ₹3,00/-.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Student.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should belong to the Adi Dravidar/ Tribal/ Adi Dravidar (converted to Christianity) community.
4 The beneficiary should have secured the highest marks in 10th or 12th standard exams within the district.
Application Process:
Step 1: The interested applicant should collect the application form from the office of the District Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Officer.
Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority.
Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission and a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. Proof of Identity (Aadhaar card).
2. Mark sheets of the 10th or 12th standard examination.
3. Community certificate (Adi Dravidar/ Tribal/ Adi Dravidar Converted to Christianity).
4. Bank Account details for prize transfer.
5. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme awards district-level prizes to top-performing Adi Dravidar, Tribal, and Adi Dravidar Converted to Christianity students. Incentives are given to one boy and one girl with the highest marks in 10th and 12th standard examinations.

Title: District Central Cooperative Banks and through its Branches: For Jewel Loan
Details: The "District Central Cooperative Banks and through its Branches: For Jewel Loan" scheme launched by the Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, Tamil Nadu, allows citizens to obtain loans by pledging their gold and jewelry. The maximum loan amount is ₹1,00,000/- with an interest rate of 12%, subject to changes as per bank policies.
Benefits:
1. Access to Loan: Up to ₹1,00,000/-.
2. Interest Rate: 12% (subject to change).
Eligibility:
1. Access to Loan: Up to ₹1,00,000/-.
2. Interest Rate: 12% (subject to change).
Application Process:
Step-1: The interested applicant should collect the application form from the District Central Cooperative Banks or its branches.
Step-2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step-3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority..
Step-4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. Identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN card, etc.).
2. Address proof.
3. Valuation certificate for the pledged jewelry.
4. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Citizens can obtain loans by pledging gold and jewelry through District Central Cooperative Banks. The scheme's objective is to provide financial assistance, with loans up to ₹1,00,000/- at 12% interest.

Title: Distribution of Nuclear Poly Hedrosis Virus
Details: The “Distribution of Nuclear Poly Hedrosis Virus” scheme by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, provides subsidies for the distribution of Nuclear Poly Hedrosis Virus (NPV) to farmers raising seed farms with Pulses crops.
Benefits: Quantum of Assistance: 50% cost of input limited to ₹250/- per hectare.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should raise seed farms with Pulses crops.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of Identity (Aadhar Card, Voter ID, etc.).
2. Proof of Land Ownership.
3. Proof of Pulses crop cultivation.
4. Caste Certificate (for SC/ST applicants).
5. Bank Account Details.
6. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Provides subsidies for the distribution of Nuclear Poly Hedrosis Virus (NPV). This scheme is for farmers in Tamil Nadu raising seed farms with Pulses crops.

Title: Quality Paddy Seed Distribution
Details: The scheme “Quality Paddy Seed Distribution”, introduced on 22nd August 2011 by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, offers a subsidy of ₹5/- per kg on certified paddy seeds. Farmers can avail this benefit when purchasing seeds from Agricultural Extension Centers. This initiative helps reduce the cost burden on farmers, encouraging them to use high-quality paddy seeds for improved crop yields.
Benefits: Financial Assistance: ₹5/- per kg subsidy on certified paddy seeds.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary must purchase certified paddy seeds from Agricultural Extension Centers.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID).
2. Land ownership documents or lease agreement.
3. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme offers farmers a ₹5/kg subsidy on certified paddy seeds purchased from Agricultural Extension Centers. Its objective is to reduce costs for farmers and encourage the use of high-quality seeds to improve crop yields.

Title: Production of Certified Seeds of Maize
Details: The scheme “Production of Certified Seeds of Maize” by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, is designed to support maize farmers in specific districts of Tamil Nadu. By offering a subsidy of ₹1,000/- per quintal, the scheme encourages farmers to produce certified maize seeds, ensuring a steady supply of high-quality seeds.
Benefits: Financial Assistance: ₹,1000/- per quintal.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should be a maize-growing farmer.
4. The beneficiary should belong to any of the following district of Tamil Nadu: Coimbatore, Dindigul, Erode, Dharmapuri, Krishnagiri, Namakkal, Perambalur, Virudhunagar, Theni, Villupuram, Vellore, Salem, Pudukkottai, Madurai, Sivagangai, Trichy, Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID)
2. Land ownership documents or lease agreement.
3. Certification of seed production.
4. Bank account details.
5. Caste certificate (if applicable).
6. Women farmer group registration documents (if applicable).
7. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme supports maize farmers in specific Tamil Nadu districts. It offers a ₹1,000/quintal subsidy to encourage certified maize seed production, ensuring a steady supply of high-quality seeds.

Title: Training to Farmers
Details: The “Training to Farmers” scheme by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, offers training to maize-growing farmers in 18 selected districts of the State. The program covers the costs of the training for up to two days, with financial assistance of  ₹300/- per farmer. The training helps farmers adopt better practices to improve yield and farm sustainability.
Benefits:
1. Financial Assistance: ₹300/- for attending a two-day training session.
2. Training Program: Training covers modern maize cultivation techniques, improving crop yield and reducing input costs.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of any of the following districts of Tamil Nadu: Coimbatore, Dindigul, Erode, Dharmapuri, Krishnagiri, Namakkal, Perambalur, Virudhunagar, Theni, Villupuram, Vellore, Salem, Pudukkottai, Madurai, Sivagangai, Trichy, Tirunelveli, and Thoothukudi.
3. The beneficiary should grow maize.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID).
2. Land ownership documents or lease agreement.
3. Caste Certificate (for SC/ST applicants).
4. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme provides training to maize-growing farmers in 18 districts of Tamil Nadu. Its main objective is to help them adopt better practices to improve yield and farm sustainability.

Title: Distribution of Gypsum-Oil Seeds
Details: The “Distribution of Gypsum-Oil Seeds” scheme by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, provides financial assistance to farmers by subsidizing 50% of the cost of gypsum material and transportation costs. The subsidy is available to farmers who produce and supply Foundation and Certified Class seeds to the Department of Agriculture.
Benefits: Financial Assistance: 50% of the cost of material plus transport limited to ₹750/- per ha whichever is less.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should be engaged in seed production.
4. The beneficiary should produce and supply Foundation and Certified Class seeds to the Department.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Identity Proof (e.g., Aadhar Card)
2. Proof of Land Ownership/Lease Agreement
3. Certificate of seed production and supply to the Department (Foundation/Certified Class).
4. Bank account details.
5. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Subsidizes 50% of gypsum material and transportation costs for farmers. It is for those who produce and supply Foundation and Certified Class seeds to the Department of Agriculture.

Title: Distribution of Manually Operated Plant Protection Equipment
Details: The “Distribution of Manually Operated Plant Protection Equipment” scheme by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, provides financial assistance to farmers by offering a subsidy for manually operated plant protection equipment. Farmers who raise seed farms with pulse crops are eligible to receive this subsidy.
Benefits: Financial Assistance: A subsidy of 50% on the cost of equipment or ₹800/- whichever is less.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should raise seed farms with Pulses crop.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of Identity (Aadhar Card, Voter ID, etc.).
2. Proof of Land Ownership.
3. Proof of Seed Farm with Pulses Crop and Bill or receipt of purchased equipment(s).
4. Caste Certificate (for SC/ST applicants).
5. Proof of being a Farm Woman (if applicable).
6. Bank Account Details.
7. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme provides financial assistance to farmers through subsidies for manually operated plant protection equipment. It is exclusively for farmers raising seed farms with pulse crops.

Title: Organizing Block Demonstration Through Department And Also Through TNAU
Details: The scheme “Organizing Block Demonstration Through Department And Also Through TNAU” by the Agriculture-Farmers Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu is designed to promote maize cultivation through block demonstrations conducted by the Department of Agriculture and Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). Farmers in select districts of Tamil Nadu can participate. It provides ₹4,000/- per demonstration for 1-hectare plots. Special focus is given to small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers.
Benefits: Financial Assistance: ₹4,000/- per demonstration of 1 Hectare plot each.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a Farmer.
2. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
3. The beneficiary should grow maize in the following districts: Coimbatore, Dindigul, Erode, Dharmapuri, Krishnagiri, Namakkal, Perambalur, Virudhunagar, Theni, Villupuram, Vellore, Salem, Pudukkottai, Madurai, Sivagangai, Trichy, Tirunelveli, and Thoothukudi.
Application Process:
Step 1: Collect the application form from the nearest Agricultural Office.
Step 2: Fill out the application form with the required details and attach mandatory documents (self-attested, if required). 
Step 3: Submit the form to the concerned office:

Village Level: Submit the application to the Assistant Agricultural Officer.
Block Level: Submit to the Agricultural Officer or Deputy Agricultural Officer.
District Level: Submit to the Joint Director of Agriculture.
documents required:
1. Proof of identity (Aadhar card, Voter ID)
2. Land ownership documents or lease agreement.
3. Proof of maize cultivation/farming.
4. Bank account details.
5. Caste certificate (if applicable).
6. Proof of small/marginal farmer status (if applicable).
7. Women farmer group registration documents (if applicable).
8. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: This scheme promotes maize cultivation through block demonstrations conducted by the Department of Agriculture and TNAU. It targets farmers in select districts of Tamil Nadu, with a special focus on small, marginal, SC/ST, and women farmers.

Title: Distribution of Iron Boxes at Free of Cost
Details: The "Distribution of Iron Boxes at Free of Cost" scheme launched by the Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu, aims to provide complimentary iron boxes to support individuals from Backward Classes (BC), Most Backward Classes (MBC), and Denotified Communities (DNCs) engaged in washing work.
Benefits: Free provision of iron boxes to eligible individuals.
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
2. The beneficiary should belong to Backward Classes (BC)/ Most Backward Classes (MBC)/ and Denotified Communities (DNCs).
3. The beneficiary should be engaged in washing work.
4. Annual income should not exceed ₹40,000/- in rural areas and ₹60,000/- in urban areas.
Application Process:
Step-1: The interested applicant should collect the application form by contacting the District Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare Officer of the concerned District.
Step-2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step-3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority.
Step-4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. Identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN card, etc.).
2. Proof of community (BC/MBC/DNC certificate).
3. Income certificate.
4. Proof of residence (Aadhaar, Voter ID, etc.).
5. Proof of occupation (if applicable).
6. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Complimentary iron boxes are provided to support individuals from Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes, and Denotified Communities engaged in washing work.

Title: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Horticulture
Details: he "Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Horticulture" scheme launched by the Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, Tamil Nadu, aims to provide financial support to farmers through loans for horticulture purposes. The loan amount varies from ₹25,000/- to  ₹2,00,000/- per 0.4 hectare, helping farmers expand or improve their horticultural activities. Interest rates range from 11% to 12.75%, subject to market conditions.
Benefits:
1. Access to Loan: From Rs.25,000/- to 2,00,000/- per 0.4 hectare.
2. Interest Rate: From 11% to 12.5%, (subject to change).
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
2. The beneficiary should be a farmer.
3. The beneficiary should be engaged in horticultural activities.
4. The beneficiary should be interested in availing loan for horticultural activities.
5. The beneficiary should have the intention to use the loan specifically for horticultural activities.
Application Process:
Step 1: The interested applicant should collect the application form by contacting the Secretary/ Special Officer the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank.
Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority.
Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. Identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN card, etc.).
2. Address proof.
3. Proof of agricultural occupation (For horticulture activities) (if applicable).
4. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Provides financial support through loans to farmers for horticulture purposes. It helps them expand or improve horticultural activities with loans from ₹25,000 to ₹2,00,000 per 0.4 hectare.

Title: District Central Cooperative Banks and through its Branches: Small Road Transport Operators Loan (SRTO Loan)
Details: The "District Central Cooperative Banks and through its Branches: Small Road Transport Operators Loan (SRTO Loan)" scheme launched by the Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, Tamil Nadu, provides loans up to ₹10,00,000/- for small road transport operations. 1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
2. The beneficiary should be a Small Road Transport Operator.
Application Process:
Step 1: The interested applicant should collect the application form from the District Central Cooperative Banks or its branches.
Step 2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step 3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority..
Step 4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, a unique identification number (if applicable).
documents required:
1. Identity proof (Aadhaar, PAN card, etc.).
2. Address proof.
3. Proof of being a Small Road Transport Operator (if applicable).
4. Any other documents (if required).
Summary: Provides loans up to ₹10,00,000 for small road transport operations. This scheme targets Small Road Transport Operators (SRTOs) through District Central Cooperative Banks.

Title: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: Jewel Loans
Details: The "Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: Jewel Loans" scheme launched by the Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection Department, Tamil Nadu, aims to provide financial assistance to farmers through jewel loans. The loan amount can be up to ₹2,00,000/-, with an interest rate of 11.5% (subject to change).
Benefits:
1. Access to Loan: Up to ₹2,00,000/- based on the value of the pledged jewels.
2. Interest Rate: 11.5% (subject to change).
Eligibility:
1. The beneficiary should be a resident of Tamil Nadu.
2. The beneficiary should be a farmer.
3. The beneficiary should be engaged in agricultural activities.
Application Process:
Step-1: The interested applicant should collect the application form by contacting the Secretary/ Special Officer of the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank.
Step-2: In the application form, fill in all the mandatory fields, paste the passport-sized photograph (signed across, if required), and attach copies of all the mandatory documents (self-attest, if required).
Step-3: Submit the duly filled and signed application form along with the documents to the concerned authority.
Step-4: Request a receipt or acknowledgment from the concerned authority to whom the application has been submitted. Ensure that the receipt contains essential details such as the date and time of submission, a unique identification number (if applicable)
documents required:
